subject: design-technology
title: Natural Fibres
welcome_lead: Cotton, wool, silk and linen — fibres from nature.
meta_desc: KS3 D&T: natural fibres, sources, uses.
final_note: Natural fibres come from plants or animals.

concepts.def: Fibre from animal hair or insect.

walkthroughs.body_html: Cotton grows in fluffy bolls on plants. Linen comes from flax stems. Both are cool, comfy and absorbent — used for T-shirts, sheets, summer clothes.
Wool is sheared from sheep — warm, springy, breathable. Silk is unwound from silkworm cocoons in China — soft, lustrous and strong for its weight.
Naturals are biodegradable and renewable, but cotton needs lots of water and pesticides. Wool can shrink in hot wash. Silk is expensive. Each has trade-offs.
